raw_response: For BNY Mellon, the 16% year-over-year decrease in reported expenses was primarily driven by the goodwill impairment associated with its investment management reporting unit in the third quarter of the prior year. In contrast, M&T Bank’s non-interest expenses decreased by $15 million sequentially due to lower compensation and benefit costs (reflecting lower average headcount and contracted resources) and lower other cost of operations (largely reflecting lower sub-advisory fees following the sale of the CIT business and lower legal-related expenses), which were partially offset by losses associated with certain retail banking activities.
